context.purpose: Compute frozen-composition ideal-gas properties, TP/HP equilibrium sweeps or closed adiabatic constant-pressure/constant-volume reactor time histories for the ten-species hydrogen/oxygen h2o2 mechanism; export independently checked numeric state tables.
context.assumptions: Isolated Cantera 3.2.x Python with the qualified h2o2.yaml SHA256. Only ideal-gas ohmech phase and its 29 reactions. SI K, Pa, kg, J, s; composition amounts are explicitly mole or mass basis and normalised. Reactors are closed, adiabatic and homogeneous with Cantera's default 1 m3 initial volume.
context.constraints: Two nodes. Sweeps: 2–100 independent temperature samples, 300–3500 K initial and final temperatures, 1000–10000000 Pa. Reactor histories: one initial temperature 300–3500 K, 2–100 strictly increasing sample times, each in seconds between 0 and 1, rtol 1e-12–1e-8, atol 1e-20–1e-12, maxSteps 100–100000 and all states within 300–3500 K. H2,H,O,O2,OH,H2O,HO2,H2O2,AR,N2 only. N2/Ar are inert; no NOx, carbon, condensed phases, transport, walls, heat loss, inflow or flames.
context.inspection: Read results.csv with numeric columns including units and X_/Y_ species fractions; reactor tables start with time_s instead of initialTemperature_K. chemistry-summary.json explains mechanism hash, phase, input basis, independent element/equilibrium/energy residuals and, for reactors, model, read-back solver settings, the declared ignition criterion and delay, and verification tolerances. Keep both when handing the table to Calc.
context.recovery: INVALID_COMPOSITION needs distinct supported species and positive total amount. INVALID_TIMES needs strictly increasing reactor sample times. INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND needs a configured Cantera Python. UNSUPPORTED_STATE means a reactor state left 300–3500 K; dilute the mixture or start colder. A changed mechanism needs explicit requalification. HP states outside 300–3500 K fail verification; choose a supported initial state/composition. Native failures retain logs; use a fresh directory after correcting input.

lifecycle.timeout: One total deadline bounds build (including the reactor sample and ignition passes) and fresh-process CSV reopen. ReactorNet maxSteps bounds each sample interval, the ignition pass stops after 200000 steps and host independent integration after 50000 steps. Kit watchdog independently bounds the entire attempt.
lifecycle.cancellation: Shared owned native process cancellation; final cancellation check precedes publication.
lifecycle.logs: authored.json, plan.json, built/reopened native records (reactor solver readback, initial mass/volume, per-sample mass/volume/net production rates and the ignition-pass step record), captured mechanism bytes/hash, worker source, stage stdout/stderr, CSV, summary and incomplete/failure results remain in each fresh attempt.
lifecycle.verification: Pure host NASA7/ideal-gas formulas verify all thermodynamic properties, normalised mass/mole fractions and element inventories. Equilibrium checks all accessible species chemical potentials against element potentials; TP holds T/P, HP holds enthalpy/P. A second Cantera process reloads the saved CSV states. No success flag substitutes for numerical checks. Reactor histories: host Python re-evaluates all 29 h2o2 rates (elementary, three-body, Troe falloff, reverse rates from NASA7 equilibrium constants) and integrates the adiabatic reactor with its own L-stable Rosenbrock method. Native and fresh-process net production rates must agree within 1e-10 of the gross rate; sampled T/X must lie within the independent solution over a 1% time window (plus 0.5 K and 1e-6); the declared ignition delay must agree within 1%; elements, mass, density (constant volume) and specific enthalpy or internal energy are conserved; solver settings and the 1 m3 initial volume are read back.

cases.scope: Monatomic ideal argon: cp=5R/(2M), cv=3R/(2M), rho=PM/(RT), h=5R(T-298.15)/(2M), X_AR=Y_AR=1. Independent literal analytic expectations.
Doubling pressure doubles ideal argon density; cp remains 5R/(2M).
Fixed T/P and normalised mass fractions are literal; independent host NASA7 chemical potentials prove equilibrium with conserved element inventories on every row.
Adiabatic equilibrium conserves initial specific enthalpy and elemental moles per kg; host NASA7 and chemical-potential checks apply to all rows. Literal initial T/P prevent a successful wrong sweep.
Independent analytic H2 dissociation extent from NASA7 Kp: alpha=sqrt(Kp/(4P/P0+Kp)), X_H=2alpha/(1+alpha). No native result is used for this expectation.
Mass amounts equal molecular weights give equimolar H2/O2 with X_H2=X_O2=0.5 and Y_H2=2.016/(2.016+31.998), at both temperature limits and the NASA7 range boundary.

Closed adiabatic stoichiometric H2/air at 1000 K and 101325 Pa. Literals are independent: initial T and pressure are authored, final specific enthalpy is the host NASA7 value of the initial state (tolerance includes the 0.19 J/kg NASA7 range-boundary jump), final T and the 400 K-rise ignition delay come from the host Rosenbrock integration of the published rates, and a zero chemical-potential residual shows the 20 ms state reached HP equilibrium.

Same mixture in a closed 1 m3 adiabatic constant-volume reactor: density stays at the initial ideal-gas value PW/(RT), specific internal energy stays at its initial NASA7 value; final T and ignition delay are independent host-integration literals.
A 1200 K start ignites about 6.7 times sooner; the delay and final T are independent host-integration literals and the final enthalpy is the initial NASA7 value (no range-boundary crossing).
Limiting case: pure argon has no reactions, so a closed adiabatic constant-volume reactor keeps T=1500 K and P=101325 Pa exactly; h=5R(T-298.15)/(2M) and cp=5R/(2M) are analytic.
